messages:
maria_se: Hey team — POC with Acme is hitting 413 when they send the full product description + attachments in one shot. Root error from gateway: `413 Payload Too Large`
customer_acme_poc: repro steps: POST /v1/generate with JSON body ~5.2MB (long context + 2 base64 images). Works fine locally but our request gets rejected by the API.
maria_se: thanks. can you paste the exact curl and response headers? quick check: are you gzipping?
customer_acme_poc: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxx" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary '@payload.json'  
Response headers: `Content-Length: 5123` `HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large`
ryan_infra: jumping in — 413 usually from our gateway nginx payload limit or cloud proxy. Two angles: reduce body size client-side (chunk or upload assets externally) or we can temporarily raise the POC body limit if justified.
sara_support: also check model-level limits — if they're sending full context as raw text, tokenization can blow past `max_context_tokens`. But 413 is before model so gateway.
james_account: if raising limit helps close the deal faster, i'm fine with a short-lived increase for the POC. we need the account id and an approved support ticket. i'll confirm pricing implications. :+1:
customer_acme_poc: would prefer not to re-architect during POC. Is there a quick workaround? signed-upload + ref IDs?
maria_se: yes — common pattern: upload large binaries to S3/GCS via signed URL, send only references (urls) in the request. for text-heavy contexts, chunk the prompt in parts and stream.
ryan_infra: sample approach: client uploads images to S3 -> include stable signed URLs in the JSON (small). For very large text, break into chunks <= 1MB and reassemble server-side or use streaming API: the request body stays small because you're streaming tokens, not full history.
sara_support: another option: enable `large_request_beta` flag on their tenant for the POC. Ops will route their traffic through a path with a raised body limit. I can open the ticket with infra if you give me account/org id.
customer_acme_poc: account id: acme-2026-01. we're okay with temporary flag. timeline: need it before EOD tomorrow.
maria_se: i'll coordinate. ryan, can you confirm safety checks required to flip the flag?
ryan_infra: safety checklist: 1) whitelist client IP CIDR for the POC; 2) enable request size increase (up to 8MB) for tenant; 3) monitor 5xx/latency for 24h; 4) have rollback plan. I'll need a ticket with the account id + contact person.
infra-bot: deploy/diff check: gateway-config change staged to canary cluster for "large_request_beta" (no rollout until approval).
sara_support: i'll create the ticket now and tag ops/infra. Also adding suggested client-side mitigations in the ticket body.
james_account: pricing note for increased egress/storage during POC — let's propose the standard POC uplift (one-off) unless they want longer-term.
customer_acme_poc: one other question — if we chunk text, how do we keep model context coherent? we need a reassembly strategy.
maria_se: short answer: either server-side concat with sliding window or use retrieval augmentation: store long docs in vector DB + send only nearest chunks as context. For immediate POC, server-side concat of chunks into one combined prompt before sending to the model works (watch token count).
sara_support: example chunking pattern we recommend (pseudocode):
```
chunks = split(long_doc, size_bytes=800000)
for each chunk:
  upload chunk metadata to POC backend
# backend concatenates latest N chunks and truncates with semantic boundary logic
# send concatenated prompt (<= max_context_tokens) to /v1/generate
```
ryan_infra: if they want to keep attachments inline (base64), we recommend compressing + multipart upload. gzip before base64 reduces payload size a lot. also prefer `Content-Encoding: gzip` + `--data-binary` so proxies see compressed body.
customer_acme_poc: any sample curl for gzip pipeline?
maria_se: sure:  
```
cat payload.json | gzip -c > payload.json.gz
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" \
  --data-binary @payload.json.gz
```
ryan_infra: note: not all proxies preserve `Content-Encoding`. the safe bet is signed upload for binaries + reference URLs.
sara_support: next steps checklist: [1] Support ticket created (S-4321) with account acme-2026-01 (link added), [2] ops to whitelist CIDR, [3] infra to toggle canary flag, [4] SE to share sample chunking + gzip curl, [5] AE shows POC uplift pricing.
maria_se: I'll drop sample code into the ticket and loop in their engineer. thanks everyone. :rocket:
customer_acme_poc: thanks all — appreciate the fast turnaround. will test signed-upload pattern first and update here later today.
